video_title: Jeezy on Young Rappers: “They’re Not Wrong, They’re Hurt”

quotes.speaker: Jeezy
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeezy on the mentorship and influence of Kevin Liles and LA Reid
quotes.excerpt: Kevin Liles is probably the only person I knew besides Secure Stewart, rest in peace Secure.
quotes.quote: When I first got signed to Def Jam, Kevin Liles and LA Reid signed me. Two weeks after they signed me, Kevin Liles is probably the only person I knew besides Secure Stewart, rest in peace Secure, because he the one that got me into Def Jam. Kevin went to Atlantic. So I was like, I need to go with you. He's like, no, you're going to be good. The next guy is coming, he's going to take care of you.

quotes.speaker: Jeezy
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeezy on the personal support he received from Jay-Z during difficult times
quotes.excerpt: A lot of that label, they wouldn't cut like Hov. Hov would literally call me.
quotes.quote: When I went through some of the most turmoil I ever felt in my life publicly, a lot of that label, they wouldn't cut like Hov. Hov would literally call me. You need to come up tomorrow, we need to talk. We would talk. Straight up. And I ain't going to lie, there's been situations I've been in where I've seen the person he is. So when I hear people say stuff, it throws me off because I'm like, dude, different.

quotes.speaker: Jeezy
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeezy on the value of receiving life advice from Jay-Z
quotes.excerpt: If it were me, and we just have a conversation. Not to say I'm going to do what he says.
quotes.quote: I can be like, what would you do? And he'd be like, man, listen, if it were me, and we just have a conversation. Not to say I'm going to do what he says, but he's giving me something I can process. It's valid advice. It's like talking to somebody who's played ball and went on with it. It's like you talking to Magic Johnson. You would say, yo Magic, look, I'm about to do this, this is what I'm thinking, what do you think?

quotes.speaker: Jeezy
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeezy on the struggles and lack of guidance for young rappers
quotes.excerpt: I think they hurt. I think they don't got no outlets. I think they don't got no big bros.
quotes.quote: I think they hurt. I think they don't got no outlets. I think they don't got no big bros like we just talking about. And I feel for them. The music is the truth. We only put in the music what we living. And I feel for them, bro. Every life is worth living. The thing that hurts me the most is to see them get there and then drop the ball because this is a once in a lifetime opportunity.

quotes.speaker: Jeezy
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeezy on why he views young rappers' behavior as pain rather than malice
quotes.excerpt: I don't look at it as if they're wrong, I look at it as if they're hurt.
quotes.quote: I don't look at it as if they're wrong, I look at it as if they're hurt. And this is what they're telling. They got to kill each other for them to feel significant. It ain't even about what I'm going to accomplish. It's about I'm significant, I can take your life. And I'm cool with that. And to me, that's who I feel like we failed them.

quotes.speaker: Jeezy
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeezy on the generational shift from survival to trauma-based pain
quotes.excerpt: Our generation was we was trying to survive. Their generation is they're trying to learn how to deal.
quotes.quote: Our generation was we was trying to survive. Their generation is they're trying to learn how to deal with all this pain, all this trauma that they got. They can't process it. Their friends are dying, their cousins are dying. And it's just like for me, I can't save everybody, but I just hope some of the things that I'm doing showing them that it's okay to grow.

quotes.speaker: Jeezy
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeezy on the difficulty of making the decision to evolve
quotes.excerpt: The hardest thing that ever happened to me in my life was having to make that decision.
quotes.quote: The hardest thing that ever happened to me in my life was having to make that decision. Boy, that was the realest decision I ever made in my life because I felt stripped of everything who I thought I was. But that's because I was walking into the man that I was becoming. But I thought that I couldn't survive without this veil around me of what I knew myself to be.
